items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And I met a lot of people there, especially one guy, a very fine friend of mine... At that time he was called Big Bill Moore; now they call him Wild Bill Moore.

ctx.x: It was during the summer when I went there, in 1940. And I started going down to the Bandbox, which was the musicians' club, where musicians would come in and hang out. And they had a piano there, and the guys would sit around and jam until the phone rang, then one of those leaders would go answer the phone, and he'd come and say, 'Well, I need a trumpet, I need a saxophone, I need a drummer, blah-blah-blah-blah' -- that's now you got gigs. So I was giggin'...got gigs that way around Detroit on the weekends.

And I met a lot of people there, especially one guy, a very fine friend of mine... At that time he was called Big Bill Moore; now they call him Wild Bill Moore. A saxophonist. I imagine you're familiar with him. And I'll talk about him later on in our California period, you know. But I was sixteen years old, you know, and I was a pretty fly little guy, you know. And the older guys, they would really put you through the test. During that time, "Liza" and "Tea For Two" and "Body and Soul," those were the tough…
